items.title: Uniqueness of a multivariate exponential transform
items.statement:
Assume AC and let $k\ge0$. Let $
u$ be a finite complex Borel measure on $\mathbb R^k$. Suppose there is $\delta>0$ such that $\int e^{\delta\|x\|_1}\,|
u|(dx)<\infty$. If the Laplace transform $L(z)=\int e^{z\cdot x}\,
u(dx)$ is zero for every real $z$ in an open neighborhood of $0$, then $
u=0$.

items.title: Likelihood-ratio equivalence on common discrete support
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal X$ be countable with its full $\sigma$-field, so it is standard Borel under the discrete metric. Let $\Theta\ne\varnothing$, and let $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ be dominated by a fixed $\sigma$-finite positive measure $\mu$. Choose the finite-valued densities $p_\theta=dP_\theta/d\mu$ as in [[def-likelihood-density]]. Let $X_0\subseteq\mathcal X$ satisfy $P_\theta(X_0)=1$ and $P_\theta(\{x\})>0$ for every $x\in X_0$ and every $\theta$. Write $m_\theta(x)=P_\theta(\{x\})$. For each $x\in X_0$, $0<\mu(\{x\})<\infty$ and $p_\theta(x)=m_\theta(x)/\mu(\{x\})$: positivity follows from $m_\theta(x)>0$, finiteness from sigma-finiteness, and the value is fixed by the density integral on the positive-measure singleton. Consequently

$$\frac{p_\theta(x)}{p_\theta(y)}=\frac{m_\theta(x)}{m_\theta(y)}\frac{\mu(\{y\})}{\mu(\{x\})}.$$

For $x,y\in X_0$, define $x\sim y$ if there is a constant $c(x,y)>0$ such that $m_\theta(x)/m_\theta(y)=c(x,y)$ for every $\theta$. The displayed fixed singleton factor shows this is equivalent to constancy of the common-reference density ratio. This is an equivalence relation: the constants for $(x,x)$, $(y,x)$ and $(x,z)$ are respectively $1$, $c(x,y)^{-1}$ and $c(x,y)c(y,z)$. Its equivalence classes form a countable quotient. Equip that quotient with its discrete $\sigma$-field; it is standard Borel because the discrete metric is complete and the countable space itself is dense. Since $\Theta\ne\varnothing$ and $P_\theta(X_0)=1$, $X_0$ is nonempty; define the class statistic by mapping each point of $X_0$ to its class and every point off $X_0$ to any fixed class. It is measurable because $\mathcal X$ has the full $\sigma$-field, and values off $X_0$ are null under every law.

items.title: A countable mixture dominates a sigma-finite dominated family
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ be a nonempty family of probability measures dominated by a $\sigma$-finite positive measure $\mu$ on $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$. There are a finite or countable sequence $(\theta_j)$ from $\Theta$ and weights $w_j>0$ summing to one such that $Q=\sum_jw_jP_{\theta_j}$ satisfies $P_\theta\ll Q$ for every $\theta$. Repetitions are permitted if $\Theta$ is finite.

items.title: Ancillary statistics
items.statement: A statistic $U:(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\to(\mathcal Z,\mathcal C)$ is **ancillary** for $(P_\theta)$ if its pushforward probability $P_\theta\circ U^{-1}$ does not depend on $\theta$. Equivalently, for every $C\in\mathcal C$, $P_\theta(U\in C)$ is constant in $\theta$.

items.title: Complete statistics
items.statement: A statistic $T:(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\to(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$ is **complete** for $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ if, for every measurable real-valued $g$ such that $E_\theta|g(T)|<\infty$ for every $\theta$, the conditions $E_\theta[g(T)]=0$ for every $\theta$ imply $P_\theta(g(T)=0)=1$ for every $\theta$. Integrability is part of the premise; completeness is a property of the statistic relative to the specified family.

items.title: Exponential families and full rank
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be standard Borel, let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-finite positive measure, let $h:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable, and let $T:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^k$ be a measurable statistic. For $\eta\in\mathbb R^k$ put

$$Z(\eta)=\int h(x)e^{\eta\cdot T(x)}\,\mu(dx),\qquad H=\{\eta:0<Z(\eta)<\infty\},\qquad A(\eta)=\log Z(\eta).$$

For a parameter set $\Omega\subseteq H$, the associated **exponential family** has laws $P_\eta$ with density

$$p_\eta(x)=h(x)\exp\{\eta\cdot T(x)-A(\eta)\}\quad(\eta\in\Omega).$$

The normalization $A(\eta)=\log Z(\eta)$ makes each density integrate to one. In this item **full-rank** means that $\Omega$ contains a nonempty open subset of $\mathbb R^k$ and there do not exist $b\ne0$ and $c\in\mathbb R$ with $b\cdot T=c$ $\mu$-almost everywhere on $\{h>0\}$. A parameter set containing an open subset is also called regular in some sources; terminology varies, so this definition controls here. The condition is stronger than needed for the completeness theorem below but rules out redundant displayed coordinates.

items.title: Sufficient statistics
items.statement:
Let $((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta))$ be a statistical experiment, where $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ is standard Borel, and let $T:(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\to(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$ be a statistic with standard Borel target. Write $P_\theta^T=P_\theta\circ T^{-1}$. The statistic $T$ is **sufficient** if there is one probability kernel $K$ from $(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$ to $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ such that, for every $\theta\in\Theta$, $A\in\mathcal A$, and $C\in\mathcal B$,

$$P_\theta(A\cap T^{-1}(C))=\int_C K(y,A)\,P_\theta^T(dy).$$

Thus $K(T(x),A)$ is a common version of the conditional probability of $A$ given $T$, under every parameter. The kernel is fixed independently of $\theta$. Under AC, standard Borelness gives each law an individual conditional law through [[thm-existence-of-regular-conditional-distributions-for-standard-borel-targets]] and [[lem-regular-conditional-kernels-factor-through-a-standard-borel-conditioning-variable]]; sufficiency additionally asks that one kernel works across parameters.

items.title: Minimal sufficient sigma-fields
items.statement:
For a family $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ on $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$, a sub-$\sigma$-field $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal A$ is **sufficient** if for every bounded measurable $u:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ there is one $\mathcal G$-measurable bounded function $v_u$ such that

$$\int_A u\,dP_\theta=\int_A v_u\,dP_\theta\quad(A\in\mathcal G,\ \theta\in\Theta).$$

For each $\theta$, this says that $v_u$ is a version of $E_\theta[u\mid\mathcal G]$, with the same pointwise version used for every parameter. Define the family-null ideal $\mathcal N=\{N\in\mathcal A:P_\theta(N)=0\text{ for every }\theta\}$. We say $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H\pmod{\mathcal N}$ if for every $A\in\mathcal G$ there is $B\in\mathcal H$ with $A\triangle B\in\mathcal N$. A sufficient $\sigma$-field $\mathcal G_*$ is **minimal sufficient** if $\mathcal G_*\subseteq\mathcal H\pmod{\mathcal N}$ for every sufficient $\mathcal H$.

items.title: Basu’s independence theorem
items.statement: Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be standard Borel, and let $T$ and $U$ be statistics from this sample space into standard Borel spaces for a family $(P_\theta)$. If $T$ is complete and sufficient and $U$ is ancillary, then $T$ and $U$ are independent under every $P_\theta$.

items.title: Common-reference factorization criterion for sufficiency
items.statement: Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and $(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$ be standard Borel, let $\Theta\ne\varnothing$, and let $T:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a statistic. Fix $\theta_0\in\Theta$ and set $P_0=P_{\theta_0}$. Assume $P_\theta\ll P_0$ for every $\theta$. Then $T$ is sufficient if and only if for every $\theta$ the Radon–Nikodym derivative $dP_\theta/dP_0$ has a $\sigma(T)$-measurable version. Equivalently, for each $\theta$ there is a Borel $g_\theta:\mathcal Y\to[0,\infty)$ with $dP_\theta/dP_0=g_\theta(T)$ $P_0$-almost surely. The null exceptional set may depend on $\theta$. The requirement $P_0\in\{P_\theta\}$ is essential; an arbitrary external dominating probability is not covered.

items.title: A full exponential family is complete
items.statement: Assume AC and let $(P_\eta)_{\eta\in\Omega}$ be a full-rank exponential family as in [[def-exponential-family]], with $\Omega$ containing a nonempty open subset of $\mathbb R^k$. Then its canonical statistic $T$ is complete.

items.title: Countable factorization criterion for sufficiency
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal X$ be a nonempty countable set with its full $\sigma$-field, let $\Theta\ne\varnothing$, let $T:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a statistic into a standard Borel space, and write $p_\theta(x)=P_\theta(\{x\})$. Then $T$ is sufficient if and only if there are nonnegative functions $h:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)$ and Borel $g_\theta:\mathcal Y\to[0,\infty)$ such that

$$p_\theta(x)=g_\theta(Tx)h(x)\quad(\theta\in\Theta,\ x\in\mathcal X).$$

The pointwise convention is $g_\theta(t)=0$ whenever $M(t)=0$, where $M(t)=\sup_{\theta}P_\theta(T=t)$ on the countable image $T(\mathcal X)$; outside that image set $g_\theta=0$.

items.title: Minimal sufficient statistics
items.statement: A statistic $T$ into a standard Borel space is **minimal sufficient** for $(P_\theta)$ if $\sigma(T)$ is a minimal sufficient $\sigma$-field in the preceding sense. Minimality is modulo sets null under every model law. It does not assert literal pointwise equality with any other minimal sufficient statistic.

items.title: The canonical statistic of an exponential family is sufficient
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $(P_\eta)_{\eta\in\Omega}$ be the exponential family of [[def-exponential-family]] on a standard Borel sample space, with $\Omega\ne\varnothing$, and let $T$ be its canonical statistic. Then $T$ is sufficient.

items.title: Standard Borel dominated factorization criterion
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and $(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$ be standard Borel, let $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ be a nonempty family dominated by a $\sigma$-finite positive measure $\mu$, and let $T:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a statistic. Then the family is dominated by a positive-weight countable mixture $Q=\sum_jw_jP_{\theta_j}$, and with $h=dQ/d\mu$, $T$ is sufficient if and only if for every $\theta$ there is a nonnegative Borel $g_\theta$ such that

$$p_\theta(x)=h(x)g_\theta(Tx)\quad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.$$

The exceptional null set may depend on $\theta$. Here $Q$ is a member of the augmented family $\{Q\}\cup\{P_\theta\}$, which is why the common-reference criterion applies. No product-density formula for a singular joint law is used.

items.title: A countable mixture likelihood-ratio vector is minimal sufficient
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $(P_k)_{k\ge1}$ be a countable family of probability measures on a standard Borel space $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$, let $w_k>0$ with $\sum_kw_k=1$, and put $Q=\sum_kw_kP_k$. Choose finite-valued Borel versions $f_k=dP_k/dQ$, changed to zero on one common $Q$-null set. Then $T(x)=(f_k(x))_{k\ge1}$ is a Borel statistic into $[0,\infty)^{\mathbb N}$ and is minimal sufficient. For every standard Borel sufficient statistic $S$, there is a Borel $\varphi$ with $T=\varphi(S)$ $Q$-almost surely.

items.title: Likelihood-ratio classes are minimal sufficient on a common discrete support
items.statement: Assume AC. Under the hypotheses of [[def-likelihood-ratio-equivalence-on-common-discrete-support]], let $T(x)=[x]_{\sim}$ on $X_0$, as a statistic into the countable quotient with its discrete standard-Borel structure, and assign one arbitrary class off $X_0$. Then $T$ is minimal sufficient for $(P_\theta)$, modulo $\mathcal X\setminus X_0$.

items.title: Two endpoint laws dominate the Bernoulli scale family
items.statement: Let $\mathcal X=\{0,1\}$ and $P_\theta=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\theta)$ for $0\le\theta\le1$. The positive mixture $Q=\tfrac12P_0+\tfrac12P_1$ dominates every $P_\theta$.

items.title: An external dominating law need not be a valid sufficiency reference
items.statement: The implication “$T$ sufficient and $P_\theta\ll R$ for every $\theta$ imply $dP_\theta/dR$ is $\sigma(T)$-measurable” is false if the reference probability $R$ is not required to belong to the family (or to share its conditional law given $T$).

items.title: Normal sample mean and residuals are independent
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be iid $N(\mu,1)$, $\mu\in\mathbb R$, with $n\ge1$. Put $\bar X=n^{-1}\sum_iX_i$ and $R=(X_i-\bar X)_{i=1}^n$. Then $\bar X$ is complete sufficient, $R$ is ancillary, and they are independent for every $\mu$.

items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be iid Bernoulli$(p)$ with $p\in(0,1)$, sample space $\{0,1\}^n$, and $T(x)=\sum_i x_i$. Then $T$ is minimal sufficient.

items.title: Likelihood-ratio vector for a point-mass model
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\mathcal X=\mathbb N_{\ge1}$ with its discrete $\sigma$-field, $P_k=\delta_k$, and $Q=\sum_{k\ge1}2^{-k}P_k$. The vector statistic $T(j)=(dP_k/dQ(j))_{k\ge1}$ is minimal sufficient and injective.
